subject: Optimize: what-if fields v1 scope (Standard Cost Model API)
body:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 29, 2026 at 9:14 AM
Subject: Optimize: what-if fields v1 scope (Standard Cost Model API)

Marissa,

Following up on yesterday’s Cost Model sync. I want to make sure Optimize’s v1 “what-if” requirements are aligned with the platform constraints before we lock schema + endpoint shapes.

Optimize v1 needs to answer (for a given workload):
1) batching: projected $/1k tokens and latency impact for target max_batch_size / max_queue_ms
2) caching: projected savings for enabling prefix/KV caching given observed prompt reuse
3) quantization: projected savings + quality guardrails by quant profile

Field asks (working draft in the doc below):
- workload summary: request_count, p50/p95 input_tokens, p50/p95 output_tokens, and prefill/decode split
- cache: observed cache hit rate OR prompt reuse proxy + whether caching is currently enabled
- batching: observed batch efficiency and queue time (if available)
- quant: model_id + candidate quantization_profile_id(s)
- deployment context: hosted/dedicated/private + hardware sku (at least family)

Main open question: can we include a “cache warm-rate” parameter as an explicit input (0..1), so we can model realistic ramp when customers turn caching on?

Doc: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1o-Optimize-CostModel-v1-Field-Requirements

If we need to cut anything for v1, I’d prefer to keep:
- prefill vs decode split (otherwise batching recommendations are mostly noise)
- a single cache effectiveness primitive (hit rate or reuse proxy)
- ability to pass a bounded list of candidate quant profiles

Thanks,
Aditya

—
Aditya Rao
Product, Redwood Optimize



From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 29, 2026 at 10:02 AM
Subject: Re: Optimize: what-if fields v1 scope (Standard Cost Model API)

Aditya,

This matches what I heard from platform. The constraints they were pretty explicit about for v1:
- request must be “small”: one workload summary object + bounded scenario list (no per-route breakdowns, no histograms)
- endpoint must be deterministic given the request + pinned schema version (finance asked for auditability)
- can’t introduce new derived parameters that are hard to validate (their example was “warm-rate”)

My suggestion for v1:
- if cache warm-rate is needed, express it as an output field (confidence interval / assumed range) rather than an input knob
- inputs should be “observables” (things telemetry can provide and we can validate)

Can you propose how you’d represent cache effectiveness without warm-rate? E.g., accept observed hit_rate (if caching already on) and otherwise accept a reuse proxy based on prompt fingerprinting?

Also: re: quantization profiles, the platform team wants a single “candidate_profile_id” per scenario (not a list) to avoid combinatorial explosion.

If you’re ok with that, we can document:
- Optimize sends N scenarios, each scenario: {batching params OR caching params OR quant_profile_id}
- cost model responds with per-scenario delta vs baseline + confidence

Marissa

—
Marissa Cole
Product, Console & Cost Visibility



From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 29, 2026 at 11:11 AM
Subject: Re: Optimize: what-if fields v1 scope (Standard Cost Model API)

Makes sense.

On caching: we can live without warm-rate as an input if we can do one of the following:
A) input: observed prefix_reuse_rate (0..1) computed over last X requests (Optimize already estimates this in our prototype)
B) input: a stable “prompt_fingerprint_coverage” + top-k reuse share (bounded) — but this may violate request size constraints

Option A is simplest and should be an “observable” if telemetry can compute it. We can define it clearly:
- prefix_reuse_rate = fraction of requests whose prompt prefix matches any of the previous M prompts within a TTL window
- M and TTL can be cost-model config (server-side), but the metric value is supplied as an input

Re: quant: ok with one candidate per scenario. Optimize can just send multiple scenarios (one per profile).

Can we align on v1 response shape for Optimize:
- baseline_estimate: cost breakdown ($ + tokens) + confidence
- scenarios[i]: delta_cost_total, delta_cost_by_component, delta_latency (if available), confidence + assumptions

I’ll update the doc to remove warm-rate input and replace with prefix_reuse_rate + note that warm behavior is captured in confidence/assumptions.

Aditya



From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 29, 2026 at 12:26 PM
Subject: Re: Optimize: what-if fields v1 scope (Standard Cost Model API)

Jumping in with a finance lens.

Two things we need for v1:
1) The output needs to explicitly separate “request-attributable” vs “allocated overhead” so we can message this correctly. The what-if deltas should, by default, apply only to request-attributable components unless the scenario explicitly changes overhead allocation (which v1 won’t).

2) For auditability, please avoid server-side “magic defaults” that aren’t discoverable. If you do keep M/TTL as server config, the response should echo the assumptions used (e.g., reuse window). It doesn’t need to be an input, but it has to be in the output.

Agree with Marissa: input knobs should be measurable. A “warm-rate” knob looks like something customers will try to game or misunderstand.

Thanks,
Laura

—
Laura Bennett
FP&A, Redwood Inference



From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 29, 2026 at 2:03 PM
Subject: Re: Optimize: what-if fields v1 scope (Standard Cost Model API)

+1 Laura’s point.

Concretely, can you update the Optimize working doc with:
- explicit definition for prefix_reuse_rate (and how Optimize calculates it today)
- a note that Cost Model API will echo its “reuse_window_seconds” assumption in the response
- scenario bounding: Optimize will send max 10 scenarios per call (we should set this expectation now)

Also, for v1, we should *not* request per-route or per-tenant segmentation in what-if; keep it one workload summary. (Console will do separate aggregation on their side.)

If you update by EOD, I’ll paste into the PRD notes and we can treat this as the v1 contract for ENG-4824 / schema review.

Marissa



From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 29, 2026 at 4:41 PM
Subject: Re: Optimize: what-if fields v1 scope (Standard Cost Model API)

Done — doc updated with the compromises and definitions.

Summary of v1 agreement (for the record):
- No cache warm-rate input knob in v1.
- Caching modeled via a single observable input: prefix_reuse_rate (0..1) + current caching_enabled.
- Quantization: one candidate quantization_profile_id per scenario; Optimize sends multiple scenarios.
- Bound requests: one workload summary + max 10 scenarios per call.
- Response must include:
  - baseline: request-attributable vs allocated overhead (separate)
  - per-scenario deltas (total + by component)
  - echoed assumptions (e.g., reuse_window_seconds) + confidence

Open items / next steps:
1) Marissa: feed this into the cost-model PRD + schema review notes.
2) Laura: if you have preferred labels for overhead components for end-user messaging, send them and we’ll align with taxonomy.
3) Me (Optimize): I’ll update our prototype client to match the “one candidate per scenario” pattern.

Thanks both.

Aditya

—
Aditya Rao
Product, Redwood Optimize
